Boundary survey

A boundary survey is a measured determination of where the legal limits of a parcel of land lie, based on the deed, the record of survey and physical evidence found in the field.

Our crews research the county records, recover existing monuments, measure the parcel, and set new monuments where the originals are missing or disturbed. The result is a signed map and a written description you can rely on in a permit application or a property dispute.

When do you need a boundary survey?

You need a boundary survey before building near a property line, before subdividing a parcel, and whenever a neighbour disputes where the line falls. Lenders and permitting offices often require one as a condition of approval.

How long does a boundary survey take?

Most residential parcels take two to three weeks from order to signed map. Rural parcels with poor record evidence take longer, because more of the work is archival research.
